howToReadThis: THE RECIPE OF THE MATTER, FROZEN, WITH THE DOUBLE READING.
Every entry carries two numbers: what the forensics SPECIFIED, and what the
targets MEASURE under an estimator that reads render and target the same way.
Where the two disagree the TARGET WINS -- a specification nobody has checked
against the picture is a requirement the picture itself may not satisfy, and
this campaign has already lost a gate to exactly that.
Every number carries the WINDOW and the METHOD it came out of. A ratio read
off an image is a property of the crop as much as of the world: three of the
entries below move by more than a tenth between two windows of open meadow,
and an entry quoted without its window is not a measurement.
Where the render cannot reach the target today, the entry carries a CEILING:
the best the render has been measured to do, and why it stops there. A gap
with a cause written beside it is work; a gap without one is an argument.
This file is a CONTRACT, not a tuning. The sessions read it before they build
and the gate judges against it. Changing a measured value means re-measuring

estimator: ricerca-demo/misure/fedelta.mjs, imported unchanged. The image is cut into
regions of near constant luminance -- in a world of flat faces a region IS a
face -- and the region means are grouped into three families by an area
weighted k-means. Reproduced verbatim on the window the demo used, which is
the check that this file is using the estimator the campaign's numbers came
from and not a second one.

why: The fitted camera of the day target, from the monolith silhouettes. It is
here because half the entries below need it: it turns a window into a piece
of GROUND, it says how many pixels a ten centimetre face should read, and it
gives a face of stone a bearing.

rocce-est.ground: the foreground stone cluster east of the eye, range about 10 m
why: The one place in either target where three orientations of ONE material can
be told apart by geometry instead of by brightness. The fitted camera says
+X projects to (117.6, 1.6) pixels per metre there and +Z to (63.7, 41.3),
so a cube's top lies above its own centre, its west face to the left and
half as wide, and its south face to the right and twice as wide -- which is
what the picture shows and what makes the ladder below a reading about
orientation rather than a sorting by luminance.

entries.what: luminance of a face by its orientation, in one material under one light

measured.rocce-est: 1.00 / 0.91 / 0.327 -- THE READING THAT WINS: the only window of either target where the three faces of one material are identified by GEOMETRY, from the fitted camera, with no clustering in the answer

note: THE THREE GRASS READINGS ARE AN ARTEFACT AND ARE KEPT AS ONE. The three
rungs of a grass window are three CLUSTERS and not three orientations: a
meadow shows tops, two flanks and a scatter of white flowers, and a k-means
with three centres has to put four populations somewhere. That is why the
middle rung moves by 0.11 between two windows of the same meadow while the
third moves by 0.02. On the rocks, where the orientation of every face is
known from the camera, the middle rung is 0.91 -- a lit vertical face stands
within a tenth of a top face in this picture, which no reading of the grass
windows shows.
AND THE RENDER READS THE SAME LADDER WITH ITS PIGMENT SWITCHED OFF: 1.000 /
0.915 / 0.330 against 1.00 / 0.91 / 0.327. The light of this world is the
light of the target and src/world/face-light.js does not change. What the
pigment does to this reading is a separate finding and it is below.
THE RUNG IS NOT INVARIANT TO THE PIGMENT, and that is why the ladder is now
quoted with the column it was read at. Carried through the frame's own chain
at the two ends of the pigment field, the bottom rung reads 0.2997 at the
darkest twentieth of columns and 0.4125 at the palest -- a spread of 0.113
against an estimator null of 0.019. tools/guards/guard-scala.mjs reads it at
the field's median and prints the two ends every run.

entries.what: the ratio between two cube tops one cube apart, at the same screen height -- how much a cube differs from the cube beside it
entries.window: finestra-demo 940, 720, 340x190; a cube is 10 px on the target and 18 here, measured
note: THE TARGET VARIES BETWEEN NEIGHBOURING CUBES MORE THAN THIS RENDER DOES, NOT
LESS, and the entry is written down because it reverses the intuition the
chequerboard produces. The prescription from the block-world literature --
keep the variation inside a material under the smallest orientation step --
is calibrated on a ladder covering 1.67x. This world and the target cover
3.06x. The target's variation sits at 63% of its own orientation step and
this render's at 45%: we were already UNDER it. What was missing was never
the amount, it was the low frequency.
AND THIS IS THE ENTRY WITH THE WORST REPEATABILITY IN THE FILE. Measured
twice on ONE state from two launches of the same build, it read 1.285 and
2.827. E-V5j's rule applies with a number: this statistic's launch-to-launch
floor is of the order of the whole gap it is being asked about, so it is a
witness and not a gate. slow-field-share above repeats to three decimals on
the same pair and is the one that carries the judgement.

entries.what: the deepest rung a cube shows: the darkest pixel under a top face over that top face, fifth percentile
entries.window: finestra-demo 940, 720, 340x190, read down each column of pixels from a local maximum

measured.the day target: 0.365 -- and 0.535 at the twenty fifth percentile

note: A FLOOR AND NOT A TARGET: the target never lets a face fall below this, so
the entry is a thing not to go under rather than a number to reach.
THE PIGMENT WAS SINKING IT AND IS NOT ANY MORE. The multiplier that shipped
covered 0.10 to 6.18 -- sixty two to one between the palest and the darkest
cube of ONE material under ONE light -- drawn independently for every cube,
so a top face and the flank under it were two independent draws and their
ratio could reach far past the light's own. The field that replaces it is a
function of the COLUMN, so that pair now shares one tint exactly and the rung
is the orientation ladder alone; and the band it may take is 0.72 to 1.72,
2.39 to one, gated in tools/guards/guard-campo-lento.mjs.
WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT THE PIGMENT'S. With the pigment switched off entirely the
same window reads 0.274 -- already under the target's 0.365 -- so the
remaining gap is the ladder and the relief, and no setting in
src/world/voxel/pigment.js reaches it.

ceiling.owner: unit A. It is what this frame reads with no pigment at all.

entries.what: how much of a meadow window the brightest family covers, and how much of its own boundary touches its own kind against a shuffle null
entries.window: finestra-demo 940, 720, 340x190; plaques segmented by gradient, three families by area-weighted k-means, null over 120 shuffles of the family labels between plaques

measured.the day target: 8.9% of the area, cohesion 66% against a null of 10 -- an excess of +56 points

note: COHESION IS THE ENTRY THAT SAYS ZONES AND SHARE IS THE ONE THAT SAYS RELIEF,
and the pass separated them by measurement. The bright family went from an
excess of +29 points over the shuffle to +55, against the target's +56: the
pale of this meadow is now a few compact patches instead of many scattered
cubes, which is what the slow field was built to do and what the pale
minority drawn per column could not.
The SHARE is a different animal. With the pigment switched off entirely the
brightest family still covers 35.3% of the window, because the share is the
ratio of top area to flank area that the eye is shown -- geometry, not
pigment. The field brings it to 21%, and the rest of the distance to the
target's 8.9% is the relief.
AND THE SPREAD INSIDE THE FAMILY REACTS BACKWARDS, which is why it is a note
and not a gate: switching OFF a source of variation used to make it rise. It
is an artefact of where the k-means cuts, not a property of the meadow.

rule: TEXTURE PER FACE WHERE THE TARGETS SHOW IT -- stone, moss, wood; on grass and
foliage the targets show a FLAT PER-VOXEL TINT and no texture at all.
Depth and unevenness are GEOMETRY: chamfers, courses, steps. Unevenness of
colour is TINT. The gate judges against the targets.

evidence: The sun of the day target stands at 47 degrees of elevation: a figure 1.8 m
tall standing on the paving must lay 1.7 m of shadow towards east-south-east.
There is none. Under the avatar's boots at the foot of the stair there is a
two pixel contact darkening and nothing else; there is none under a block of
stone on the meadow either, nor under the monoliths. The sun's bearing was
read off the LIT FACES precisely because there was no shadow to read it from.
This render has none by protocol: src/core/renderer.js sets shadowMap.enabled
to false, the one line at run time in the whole repository. The seven
occurrences of castShadowTest are an OFFLINE fitting instrument and not a
shadow map.
The entry is written because the two pictures agree and the absence is worth
three to four depth-only passes a frame. It is the dearest thing this world
can go on NOT buying, and without a line here somebody eventually builds it.

absencesToDefend.verdict: absent, and forbidden BY MEASUREMENT before it is forbidden by cost
evidence: The border profile -- luminance against distance from a face's own edge, on
its own inside -- is flat to within 1.2% out to 6 px in both pictures: the
Vertex ambient occlusion in the canonical form -- Lysenko, 0 FPS, 2013, four
discrete levels interpolated across the quad -- maps an occluded vertex onto
a ramp of about 28% over 6 px on a 16 px face. The target is roughly TWENTY
EIGHT TIMES flatter than that technique permits. It is not an opinion about
the cost: it is the measurement saying the technique is not in the picture.
The cost is the second reason and it is large: vertex AO can only be merged
where the four corners agree, and greedy meshing is worth 2.3x to 3.3x on the
geometry of a world like this one.
The only edge darkening either picture has is the JOINT, and it has its own
entry: 6% over one or two pixels. A line, not a well.

absencesToDefend.evidence: the border profile is flat to within 0.008 out to 6 px from a face's own edge, in both targets
sub-pixel 50% crossings on 17 silhouette edges spread across the frame: red minus green 0.041 px, blue minus green -0.032 px
a still frame cannot show one; kept as a rule rather than a measurement

absencesToDefend.verdict: PRESENT, measured -- and the campaign's amendment says it is not
evidence: Clear sky only, binned by the ELEVATION the fitted camera gives each pixel,
so the sky's own gradient with height is out of the comparison. At 16 deg of
elevation the day target reads 66 at the left eighth of the frame, 112 to 133
across the middle and 82 at the right eighth: half the light at one edge and
six tenths at the other. The night target has the same shape -- 12, 19 to 22,
It cannot be the sky's own azimuthal gradient. The frame spans bearings 317
to 38 and the sun stands at 280, so the sky would be BRIGHTEST at the left
edge, 37 deg off the sun, and darkest at the right, 118 deg off it. It reads
the other way round and falls off on both sides at once, which no sky does
and every lens does.
And the shape is familiar: the historic reference's own fitted veil wanted
0.23 at the upper left corner and 0.46 at the upper right -- darker on the
left, exactly as measured here. These targets appear to carry the same corner
shading the photorealistic reference did.
RAISED, NOT DECIDED. Whether to reproduce it is the coordinator's, and the
amendment that says the targets have no vignette was written before this
measurement existed.
DECIDED FOR THE GATES, THOUGH, AND UNTIL V9: it is carried as a transitory
veil and refitted in V9, so every session comparison DIVIDES IT OUT or is
read as a ratio inside one band of the frame -- which is what makes a
reading of the corner eighths mean anything at all. No crop of the left or
right horizon can be judged without this rule, because the render has no
corner shading anywhere outside the spawn; whether the picture ends up
carrying the veil is the question V9 answers.

architecture: Never a per-voxel property inside a vertex attribute. Measured violation: 3.0x the geometry of the world.

ONE step, 0.10 m, and no ring scale, ON THE WALKABLE DISC. Rings anchored to the world are false as soon as the walker moves: 11x of apparent size error, measured. The ban is on RINGS, and it stays exactly where it was written.

THE CORNICE PAST 100 m IS NOT ON THAT STEP, and the line above never meant it was. Measured on the targets, the apparent rise of a ridge is 0.16-0.37 deg, which at the distances in play is 0.3-2.7 m of cube -- a tenth of a metre would want the ridge at nineteen metres. So the far frame is built of BIGGER CUBES PLANTED IN THE WORLD, whose size is a property of the ground they stand on and not of where the walker is standing; that is what makes them not a ring scale. The distinction was always intended and was never written down, and the first session to lay a block past the shell hit it.
bakedLight() stays at two terms, bit for bit, with one producer: src/world/face-light.js.

warning: THE ESTIMATOR DOES NOT READ THE NIGHT TARGET'S MATERIAL, and that is worth
knowing before somebody quotes a number off it. Its brightest family comes out
at 252,248,239 with a spread of 0.2 per cent: those are the lamps and their
haloes, saturated, not cube tops. The ladder, the tint and the joint of the
night target are therefore not readings about the matter -- only the rise and
the border profile survive, and both are quoted above.
V7 needs a window with no point light in it, or its own estimator.
